territorial_scope.description: Applies to assessment mechanisms and providers for eye assessments and prescriptions in Rhode Island, a US state.

agora_applications: Medicine, life sciences and public health

summary.short: Rhode Island statute regulating eye assessments and prescriptions for contact lenses and visual aid glasses made through assessment mechanisms, including AI devices. Requires licensed providers to meet in-person examination and disclosure conditions, sets a civil penalty of up to $10,000 per violation, and takes effect upon passage.
summary.long: The Consumer Protection in Eye Care Act regulates assessment mechanisms, defined to include artificial intelligence devices, used to conduct eye assessments or generate prescriptions for contact lenses or visual aid glasses in Rhode Island. Mechanisms must allow synchronous or asynchronous provider-patient interaction, collect medical history and prior prescription data, and disclose to patients, as a term of use, that the assessment does not replace an in-person comprehensive eye examination and cannot generate an initial contact lens prescription. An assessment may be used for visual aid glasses only if the patient had an in-person comprehensive eye examination within the previous twenty-four months. Providers must be actively licensed, meet in-person standards of care, not rely on assessment data as the sole basis for a prescription, verify patient identity and that the patient is at least eighteen, keep medical records, and certify with their state license number. Any person violating the chapter or Department of Health rules faces a civil penalty of up to $10,000 per violation, with an administrative hearing and appeal of final orders to superior court. The Department of Health must adopt implementing rules. The act takes effect upon passage.

notes: The text contains no bill number, sponsor or adoption date; SECTION 2 states only that the act takes effect upon passage. The operative addressees are 'person' and 'provider' as defined, and no named firm or facility appears. The 'Prescription' definition incorporates federal rules by reference. No internal inconsistency was found; the 24-month in-person examination periods in 23-97-3(a)(3)(iii), 23-97-4(a)(6) and 23-97-4(a)(7) are consistent with each other.

"Assessment mechanism" means automated or virtual equipment, application, or technology designed to be used on a telephone, a computer, or an Internet-accessible device
"Contact lens" means any lens placed directly on the surface of the eye, regardless of whether or not it is intended to correct a visual defect
"Eye assessment" means an assessment of the ocular health and visual status of a patient that may include
"Person" means an individual, corporation, trust, partnership, incorporated or unincorporated association, and any other legal entity.
"Prescription" means a handwritten or electronic order issued by a provider that includes:
"Provider" means a health care professional licensed under chapters 35.1 or 37 of title 5 of the general laws.
"Visual aid glasses" means eyeglasses, spectacles, or lenses designed or used to correct visual defects

obligations.summary: An assessment mechanism used for an eye assessment or prescription in Rhode Island must provide synchronous or asynchronous interaction between patient and provider, and must collect the patient's medical history, previous corrective eyewear prescription, and time since the last in-person comprehensive eye health examination (23-97-3(a)(1)-(2)).

evidence.quote: Provide synchronous or asynchronous interaction between the patient and the provider;

obligations.summary: Must disclose to patients, and require acceptance in advance as a term of use, that the assessment is not a replacement for an in-person comprehensive eye health examination; cannot generate an initial contact lens prescription or a follow-up or first renewal; may be used for visual aid glasses or contact lens prescriptions only if the patient had an in-person examination within the previous 24 months; and that CDC advises annual eye visits for contact lens wearers.

evidence.quote: Disclose to patients and require acceptance in advance as a term of use that:

obligations.summary: To use an assessment mechanism for an eye assessment or prescription, the person must be an actively licensed provider acting within their scope of practice.

evidence.quote: a person shall be an actively licensed provider acting within their scope of practice

obligations.summary: Provider must conform to the standard of eye health care expected of traditional in-person clinical settings, appropriate to patient age and condition, including diagnostic testing and physical examination where the standard of care requires, which may use peripheral devices.

evidence.quote: Conform to the standard of eye health care expected of traditional in-person clinical settings

obligations.summary: Provider must read and interpret the diagnostic information and data, including photographs and scans, gathered by the assessment mechanism. Also shall not use data or information from an eye assessment as the sole basis for issuing a prescription (23-97-4(a)(2)).

evidence.quote: Read and interpret the diagnostic information and data, including any photographs and scans, gathered by the assessment mechanism.

obligations.summary: Provider must verify the patient's identity, verify the patient is at least 18 years old, verify an in-person comprehensive eye examination within 24 months before prescribing visual aid glasses, and verify in-person examinations for contact lens prescriptions at the initial prescription, at the first follow-up or renewal, and every 24 months thereafter (23-97-4(a)(4)-(7)).

evidence.quote: Verify the identity of the patient requesting treatment via the assessment mechanism.

obligations.summary: Provider must create and maintain a medical record for each patient for use during ongoing treatment, complying with state and federal laws on maintenance and accessibility.

evidence.quote: Create and maintain a medical record for each patient

obligations.summary: Provider must provide a handwritten or electronic signature, with their Rhode Island state license number, certifying the diagnosis, evaluation, treatment, prescription, or consultation recommendations.

evidence.quote: Provide a handwritten or electronic signature, along with their Rhode Island state license number
